articleSummary: Mpox (formerly monkeypox) is caused by mpox virus. articleHeadline: Africa: Conflicts Can Spread Infectious Diseases While Making Outbreaks Harder to Detect
articleSummary: Conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, extending into Uganda, coincided with an Ebola outbreak that MSF says killed at least 55 people since April 2026; alarm was raised in May, and on May 17 the WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern. This event sits within a broader analysis of outbreaks reported to WHO’s Disease Outbreak News (1996–2024) and their relation to armed conflict across 236 countries, showing war can spread disease by destroying health services and vaccination and by displacing people, while also making detection harder. Examples: polio outbreaks are more common during civil wars due to disrupted vaccination; wild poliovirus remains in Afghanistan and Pakistan; cholera outbreaks tend to rise one to two years after fighting begins, with Yemen contributing a major epidemic (>1 million suspected cases). articleSummary: Isolated orbital histoplasmosis, a rare fungal infection of the tissues around the eye, was diagnosed and treated in an immunocompetent patient at Artemis Hospitals, India. The presenting complaint was a persistently red eye with eye discomfort that did not respond to standard therapies. Histoplasma capsulatum, typically associated with pulmonary disease, can arise in soil contaminated with bird or bat excreta; orbital involvement in an otherwise healthy individual is exceedingly rare. Diagnosis was confirmed by tissue biopsy after unresponsiveness to conventional treatment. The patient received antifungal therapy guided by the infectious diseases team, with drug selection, dosing, and duration tailored to clinical response due to limited ocular penetration and lack of standard guidelines. Treatment continued for nearly a year, culminating in resolution of symptoms and maintained vision. The case underscores the value of early biopsy and a multidisciplinary approach when orbital infections mimic other conditions.

Humans acquire infection through contact with contaminated water or mud via broken skin or mucous membranes, ingestion of contaminated food or water, or contact with infected animals. articleSummary: The fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history is unfolding in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with 3,442 cases and 1,521 deaths reported as of the latest update (published 2026-07-30). About 797 patients are isolated or hospitalized and 615 have recovered; contact tracing covers roughly 78% of known contacts, well below the 95% target needed to halt transmission. articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 3,442 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,521 deaths as of July 28, 2026, with a 44.2% case fatality rate. This is the 17th epidemic in the DRC, which began May 15 in Ituri and spans five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain drives a CFR of 30–50% and, per WHO, has no approved vaccine or specific treatment. Uganda reported 20 cases and two deaths, with the country declared Ebola-free on July 28 after 42 days without local transmission, following the last patient’s discharge on July 16; 15 of Uganda’s cases were imported from the DRC. Response challenges include security for teams, contact tracing, treatment-center capacity, and supplies (797 in isolation/hospitalization; 615 recoveries; 78.3% contact-tracing rate). The outbreak lags behind the 2018–2020 DRC surge (2,299 deaths, 3,481 cases) and the West Africa 2014–2016 epidemic (~11,000 deaths, 28,000 cases).

articleHeadline: Ghana: Hepatitis B - Ghana Cannot Afford a Silent Crisis
articleSummary: Ghana faces a silent hepatitis crisis: ~3 million people live with chronic hepatitis B, with <1% diagnosed and <1% of those diagnosed receiving treatment. During World Hepatitis Day, the Ghana Health Service highlighted the gap as hepatitis B deaths rose from 15,443 in 2024 to about 16,000 in 2025; hepatitis C deaths also increased. To reach WHO targets of diagnosing 90% and treating 80% by 2030, Ghana plans a nationwide birth-dose vaccination program, vaccine coverage for the third HBV dose at ~95% among infants, expanded screening, stronger surveillance, and decentralised services. Mother-to-child transmission accounts for ~95% of HBV infections; high-prevalence regions include Savannah, Northern, Upper West, and Upper East. The Technical Working Group on viral hepatitis will focus on expanding testing, improving treatment access, and monitoring progress. Public awareness and sustained investment are urged to convert words into action.

articleSummary: As of July 30, 2026, Kisangani’s Lubunga urban-rural commune in the Tshopo province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains divided between skepticism and precaution over Ebola virus disease. Despite being among the most affected areas, residents report no visible cases and demand tangible manifestations before accepting the outbreak. Preventive measures—handwashing, avoiding handshakes, and avoiding contact with bodies of unknown causes of death—are promoted, but market and street-level visibility is low, with scarce handwashing facilities and few information posters. Market traders and residents say information mainly comes from media, not authorities, and some doubt the disease is present locally. The Lubunga health zone has recorded one confirmed imported Ebola case, part of six imported cases from Ituri province reported in Kisangani since the start of the flare-up. articleSummary: Dengue fever deaths in Indonesia are heavily concentrated in children. articleSummary: A Shanghai man contracted Entamoeba histolytica after consuming large amounts of raw, spiced seafood during a trip to Thailand, triggering a life-threatening amebic infection with widespread intestinal ulcers, heavy bleeding, and septic shock. The report also warns that other raw or undercooked foods and unboiled water can transmit the parasite. Five travel safety rules include cooking thoroughly, drinking bottled water, choosing reputable venues, hand hygiene, and seeking prompt medical care if symptoms arise after seafood consumption.
